title: The Alarm Beyond the Wall — Post-Storm Portable Generator Exhaust Aerodynamics (167 Florida Cases, 16 Outdoor vs. 16 Garage), Wind-Wake Infiltration, Pulse Oximetry SpO2 Blindness & Battery CO Alarms

teenKit.tldr: When the power grid goes down after a storm, portable generators create a silent, invisible killer called carbon monoxide that can track wind currents right back into your house. Even scariest, standard medical monitors and dead batteries can leave you completely blind to the danger.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how invisible gas flows and how medical tech fails can literally save your life during the deadliest, most overlooked phase of a natural disaster.
keyTakeaways: Generators placed completely outside can still poison a home because wind turbulence creates an aerodynamic wake that sucks exhaust directly through open windows or AC units.
Standard hospital pulse oximeters measure oxygen using two light wavelengths, which accidentally mistakes carbon monoxide for healthy oxygen and gives a dangerously false sense of security.
Household carbon monoxide alarms rely entirely on backup batteries during grid failures, meaning dead or forgotten batteries turn life-saving safety devices into silent paperweights.

vocab.meaning: A colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas produced by burning fuel that starves your organs of oxygen by binding tightly to your red blood cells.
An aerodynamic phenomenon where wind flowing around a house creates a low-pressure pocket that sucks outside exhaust fumes right back through cracks and openings.
A medical limitation where standard fingertip oxygen sensors cannot tell the difference between oxygen and carbon monoxide in the bloodstream.
An advanced medical blood test that uses multiple wavelengths of light to accurately measure how much carbon monoxide is actually poisoning the blood.

quiz.question: If you place a portable generator completely outside your home after a storm, why is it still capable of poisoning you?
options: The generator's electricity creates toxic ions in the air.
Wind aerodynamics can create a wake that sucks the exhaust fumes directly back into the house through windows or AC units.
The sound waves from the generator pull air backward.
Cold outside air naturally forces exhaust downward into the soil.
quiz.explanation: Wind patterns and pressure differences around buildings can trap and pull outdoor exhaust right through structural openings.

quiz.question: Why does a standard fingertip pulse oximeter often fail to detect carbon monoxide poisoning?
options: It requires a battery voltage that drops during power outages.
It only measures skin temperature instead of blood chemistry.
It uses two light wavelengths that misread carbon monoxide molecules as normal oxygen-carrying hemoglobin.
It is programmed to shut off automatically after 10 minutes.
quiz.explanation: Standard oximeters read carbon monoxide the exact same way they read oxygen, giving a falsely high and misleading health reading.

quiz.question: According to the episode, what makes the post-storm period so uniquely dangerous compared to the actual hurricane?
options: Floodwaters rise faster after the wind stops.
People let their guard down and deploy emergency tools like generators that introduce hidden technological hazards.
Hospital emergency rooms completely close down for days.
Wildlife is forced out of hiding by the silence.
quiz.explanation: The transition from natural disaster to the quiet aftermath causes people to deploy invisible hazards like generators without realizing the risks.
